chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Muhammad ibn Ziyad and Safwan from Rifa'ah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who divorced his wife until she became completely separated from him and her waiting period ended, then she married another husband, and he also divorced her, then she married her first husband again. Does that [subsequent marriage and divorce] invalidate the first divorce? He said, 'Yes.'

Ibn Sama'ah said: And Ibn Bukayr used to say: If a divorced woman is divorced by her husband, then he leaves her until she becomes completely separated, then he marries her, she is with him upon a new divorce.

Ibn Sama'ah said: And Al-Husayn ibn Hashim mentioned that he asked Ibn Bukayr about it, and he answered him with this answer. He said to him, 'Did you hear anything regarding this?' He said, 'The narration of Rifa'ah.'
So he said: Indeed Rifa'ah narrated that when a husband enters between them, he said, 'A husband and a non-husband are equal in my view.'
So I said, 'Did you hear anything regarding this?' He said, 'No, this is what Allah granted him of opinion (ijtihad).'
Ibn Sama'ah said: And we do not take the opinion of Ibn Bukayr, for the narration [of Rifa'ah] is that when a husband enters between them.

key_terms.بَانَتْ: To become completely separated/divorced (finality of divorce)
key_terms.رِفَاعَةَ: Rifa'ah ibn Sa'd, a key narrator

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a woman returning to her first husband after a triple divorce in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the mechanism of 'Iddah al-Talaq' (divorce waiting period) and the validity of remarriage after a final divorce, specifically addressing whether a subsequent marriage to a third party is required to 'undo' the initial divorce. It highlights the scholarly debate between the authoritative narration of Rifa'ah and the juristic opinion (ra'y) of Ibn Bukayr, ultimately affirming that the third marriage serves as the necessary bridge for the first couple to reunite. This discussion is central to Shia fiqh regarding the conditions under which a wife becomes lawful again to her first husband after a triple divorce.
